R03 · Conservative English prose editing with a fact ledger

V1.0 · research track · difficulty 3/5 · suggested budget 30 minutes.

Working contract. This is a self-contained candidate task. Work only from the supplied materials; cite embedded source identifiers and locations. You may use local libraries and code. Do not fetch additional papers, assets, fonts, services, or model outputs. State any local runtime limitation. All scientific examples and numerical fixtures created by the benchmark are synthetic and are labelled as such. No hidden answer file is needed.

Editing assignment

A collaborator wants the following English manuscript passage to read naturally and precisely. Edit it conservatively for a methods/results audience. The task is editorial: improve the prose while preserving the scientific record and handling unsupported claims transparently. No AI detector, detector score or promise of “undetectability” is part of the task.

Author-approved factual record

The numbers in this record belong to this editing task and must not be recomputed from another benchmark question. There were twelve independent devices, three batches, four devices per batch, paired once before and once after a 10 minute conditioning step at 25 °C. Rounded group means were 1000.4 and 1001.6 mV; the mean paired increase was 1.2 mV. The author reports a two-sided paired test with p = 0.08 but has not supplied the test family, statistic or interval. Measurements were recorded to 0.1 mV; calibration uncertainty is unknown. A separate six-device transient experiment had two devices per batch; input was stepped at 0 s and held through 12 s. The normalized response approached unity. No later times, mechanism experiment, long-term stability data, or deployment test were collected. The author intends to propose calibration checks and longer observation windows as future work. No citation has been supplied.

Draft to edit

In the rapidly evolving landscape of sensor science, conditioning emerges as a pivotal strategy for unlocking robust device performance. Here, we delve into a comprehensive assessment of twelve independent devices fabricated across three batches, with four devices in each batch. Each device was measured once before and once after a ten-minute conditioning step at 25 °C. The potential increased by 1.2 mV on average, from 1000.4 to 1001.6 mV, and the two-sided paired test gave p = 0.08. This demonstrates a transformative and statistically significant enhancement.

It is important to note that the measurements were recorded to 0.1 mV, while the instrument's calibration uncertainty was not available. The same devices were measured twice, and no new device was introduced after conditioning. A separate experiment comprised six independent devices, two from each batch. The input was stepped at zero seconds and held for twelve seconds, during which the normalized signal approached unity. It is not merely a response; it is a testament to the stability of the system. No measurements were made after twelve seconds. These findings underscore the vast potential of this approach for long-term deployment and establish the conditioning mechanism. Taken together, the results reveal small short-term changes under the tested conditions. Future work should include calibration checks and longer observation windows.

Deliverables

  1. Provide a polished 180–250 word English passage suitable for the manuscript. You may reorganize sentences and remove repetition. Keep the quantitative record, experimental units, pairing, missing uncertainty, temporal limits and future-work status intact. Resolve unsupported wording through a clearly documented editorial change or a specific author query; do not create new evidence.
  2. Create a fact ledger with one row per material claim. Record the original wording or claim ID, factual status, edited location and disposition: preserved, clarified, removed as unsupported, or queried. Include numbers, uncertainty, scope, causality and significance claims.
  3. Provide a short edit memo explaining the highest-impact changes and any unresolved author queries. Distinguish language editing from scientific verification; do not certify results that the supplied record cannot verify.

Submission contract

Place the following durable files in your submission directory. Use relative local links and include commands and dependency versions needed to regenerate outputs. The written work should stand on its own; screenshots alone do not replace editable sources.

  • edited.md
  • fact-ledger.csv
  • edit-memo.md

Core requirements

These are reported individually as met, not met, or not assessable. A high numeric score does not override a failed core requirement.

  • Material quantitative and experimental facts remain faithful to the approved record.
  • Unsupported significance, causality and duration claims are handled explicitly without adding evidence.
  • A claim-by-claim fact ledger accompanies the edited passage.
